course_name_original: Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales II
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II
prerequisites: ELASTICIDAD Y RESISTENCIA DE MATERIALES I

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; choose and apply appropriately established analytical, computational and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of said analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; choose and apply appropriate established analytical, computational and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to plan, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems in their specialty, which meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Engineering projects: Project ability using some cutting-edge knowledge of their engineering specialty.

Research and innovation: Ability to conduct bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Capacity and skill to design and carry out experimental research, interpret results and reach conclusions in their field of study.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and analysis, design and research methods and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment formulation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in a team, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Continuous training: Ability to recognize the need for one's own continuous training and to undertake this activity throughout one's professional life independently.
Continuous training: Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Define the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each one, and making correct use of language, in writing.

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, presentation and technical defense
Written and oral individual tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For certain outcomes, if continuous assessment (C) is greater than 4, the grade (N) is calculated as 75% of C plus 25% of individual tests (E). If N is less than 5, or if C is less than 4, a resit (R) is required. The final grade (Nf) after a resit is calculated as 25% of the initial grade (N or C) plus 75% of the resit grade (R). Continuous evaluation and feedback are provided for project-based assessments.
